question: What is a bit?
reference: A binary digit representing one of two values, conventionally zero and one.
title: Course reference

question: What is a byte?
reference: In modern usage, a group of eight bits.
title: Course reference

question: What is a transparent D latch?
reference: A level-sensitive one-bit store; while enabled Q follows D after delay, otherwise it holds its value.
title: Course reference

question: What is a positive-edge D flip-flop?
reference: It samples D on a rising clock edge and holds Q between rising edges, assuming setup/hold requirements.
title: Course reference

question: Define setup time for a flip-flop.
reference: The minimum time data must be stable before the active sampling edge.
title: Course reference

question: Define hold time for a flip-flop.
reference: The minimum time data must remain stable after the active sampling edge.
title: Course reference

question: What is metastability in a flip-flop?
reference: An unstable intermediate internal state with abnormally long settling; violation does not guarantee an opposite bit.
title: Course reference

question: What is a stack data structure?
reference: Last in, first out; push and pop operate on the same end.
title: Course reference

question: What is a queue data structure?
reference: First in, first out; enqueue and dequeue use logically opposite ends.
title: Course reference

question: What is an integer?
reference: A whole number including zero and negative whole numbers; no fractional part.
title: Course reference

question: What is binary search?
reference: Searches ordered data by repeatedly halving the candidate interval; logarithmic comparisons with random access.
title: Course reference

question: What is a stable sorting algorithm?
reference: Preserves the original relative order of records having equal sort keys.
title: Course reference

question: Define sampling frequency.
reference: The number of samples taken per unit time, usually samples per second or hertz.
title: Course reference

question: What is aliasing in sampled signals?
reference: Different continuous frequencies can produce indistinguishable sample sequences; insufficient sampling can fold frequencies.
title: Course reference

question: What is a series circuit connection?
reference: Components share a single current path, so the same current passes through them.
title: Course reference

question: What is a parallel circuit connection?
reference: Components connect across the same pair of nodes and have the same voltage across them.
title: Course reference

question: What is an ideal capacitor?
reference: Stores energy in an electric field; Q=CV and i=C dv/dt for constant capacitance.
title: Course reference

question: What is an ideal inductor?
reference: Stores energy in a magnetic field; v=L di/dt for constant inductance.
title: Course reference

question: Define the derivative of a function at a point.
reference: The limit of the difference quotient when it exists; the instantaneous rate of change or tangent slope.
title: Course reference

question: What does algorithmic time complexity describe?
reference: How computational work scales with input size under a specified model; not the exact wall-clock runtime.
title: Course reference

question: Explain how a D latch differs from a D flip-flop, including setup and hold time.
reference: Latch transparent while enabled; flip-flop samples an edge. Setup before, hold after capture; latch timing is around closing enable.
title: Course reference

question: Explain the difference between a primary key and a foreign key in a relational database.
reference: Primary key uniquely identifies a row and is non-null; foreign key references a permitted key and enforces referential integrity subject to null rules.
title: Course reference

question: Explain linear independence of a set of vectors.
reference: Only the all-zero coefficients make their linear combination zero; no vector is a redundant combination of the others in an independent set.
title: Course reference

question: What is the difference between precision and recall in binary classification?
reference: Precision TP/(TP+FP); recall TP/(TP+FN). Mention undefined denominator handling if relevant; do not reverse them.
title: Course reference

question: Explain the difference between resistance and impedance in AC circuits.
reference: Resistance is the real dissipative component; impedance is generally complex and includes reactance with magnitude and phase, depending on frequency.
title: Course reference

question: What is the difference between compilation and interpretation?
reference: Compilation translates code before or during execution; interpretation executes via another program. JIT and hybrids exist; languages need not be inherently one or the other.
title: Course reference

question: Explain conservation of energy in an ideal closed system.
reference: Total energy remains constant while changing forms; disappearance of useful mechanical energy can be conversion to heat rather than destruction.
title: Course reference

question: What is the difference between lexical and semantic search?
reference: Lexical search matches words; semantic search matches representations of meaning. Neither guarantees relevance; hybrid can combine them.
title: Course reference

question: Explain one's complement versus two's complement for signed binary integers.
reference: One's complement negates by bit inversion and has two zeros; two's complement adds one after inversion and has a single zero, with asymmetric signed range.
title: Course reference

question: Explain necessary and sufficient conditions using implications.
reference: P sufficient for Q means P implies Q; P necessary for Q means Q implies P; both means equivalence.
title: Course reference

question: Explain causality versus BIBO stability for a discrete-time system.
reference: Causality means no dependence on future input; BIBO stability means every bounded input yields bounded output. Neither implies the other in general.
title: Course reference

question: What is the relationship between a square matrix's determinant and invertibility?
reference: Over a field, a square matrix is invertible exactly when its determinant is nonzero; determinant zero means singular.
title: Course reference

question: Explain serial versus parallel loading of a register.
reference: Serial transfers bits sequentially through a serial input; parallel loading captures multiple bits together on the loading event.
title: Course reference

question: Does negative feedback always make a system stable? Explain.
reference: No. Loop gain, phase shift, dynamics and delays matter; nominal negative feedback can become reinforcing at relevant frequencies.
title: Course reference

question: What is the difference between an ideal open circuit and an ideal short circuit?
reference: Open circuit carries zero current but may have voltage; ideal short has zero voltage but may carry current. Do not reverse these.
title: Course reference

question: What does a p-value mean, and is it the probability the null hypothesis is true?
reference: It measures probability under the null model of outcomes at least as extreme by the specified test; not the probability the null is true.
title: Course reference

question: Explain covariance versus correlation.
reference: Covariance measures joint variation in units of the variables; Pearson correlation normalizes by standard deviations and is unitless, undefined for zero variance.
title: Course reference

question: What is the difference between prompt caching and retrieval in an AI application?
reference: Prompt caching reuses computation for repeated input prefixes; retrieval selects relevant external evidence. Caching does not guarantee the answer itself is reused.
title: Course reference

question: Explain blocking versus nonblocking I/O.
reference: Blocking waits for an operation to become ready/complete; nonblocking returns promptly with available progress or an indication it would block. Async is related but not identical.
title: Course reference

question: What is the difference between an idempotent operation and a pure function?
reference: Repeated idempotent application has the same relevant effect as one application; purity concerns deterministic results and absence of observable side effects. They are different properties.
title: Course reference

reference: 10/sqrt(2) V, approximately 7.071 V.

reference: x < -2; reverse the inequality when dividing by -2.

question: Simplify Boolean A B + A NOT B and identify the law.
reference: A, using distributivity and B OR NOT B = 1.

question: Solve sqrt(x+1) = x-1 over the reals and reject extraneous candidates.
reference: x >= 1 initially. Squaring gives candidates 0 and 3. Only 3 satisfies the original equation.

question: Differentiate ln(3x+1) and state its real domain.
reference: Derivative 3/(3x+1), original real domain x > -1/3.

question: Calculate the total capacitance of 6 microfarads and 3 microfarads in series.
reference: 2 microfarads.

title: Course reference

question: Calculate P(A given B) if P(A and B)=0.12 and P(B)=0.3.
reference: 0.4, since conditional probability is the intersection divided by P(B).
title: Course reference

question: Calculate the slope and y-intercept of the line through (1,3) and (3,7).
reference: Slope 2 and intercept 1; y=2x+1.

question: Solve absolute value of x minus two less than three.
reference: If the expression is |x-2| < 3, then -1 < x < 5. State that interpretation.

question: Evaluate a positive-edge D flip-flop: Q starts 0, D is 1 at the rising edge, then D becomes 0 before the falling edge. What is Q after falling?
reference: Q=1 if timing requirements are met; the falling edge does not sample D.

question: Prove by induction that the sum of the first n odd positive integers is n squared.
reference: Base case n=1; add 2n+1 to n squared to get (n+1) squared.
title: Course reference

question: Derive the energy stored in an ideal capacitor from charge and voltage.
reference: Integrate v dq with v=q/C from 0 to Q to get Q squared/(2C)=CV squared/2.
title: Course reference

question: Derive the continuous Fourier transform of exp(-a t) u(t) for real a>0, using exp(-j omega t).
reference: Integral from zero to infinity yields 1/(a+j omega), convergence requires a>0.
title: Course reference

question: Prove that the square root of two is irrational.
reference: Assume a reduced integer ratio; squaring makes numerator even, then denominator even, contradicting coprimality.
title: Course reference

question: Calculate eigenvalues of the diagonal matrix with diagonal entries 2 and 3.
reference: 2 and 3.
title: Course reference

question: Solve the differential equation y'=y with y(0)=2.
reference: y=2 exp(t).
title: Course reference

question: Prove that the derivative of a differentiable even function is odd wherever the reflected points are in its domain.
reference: Differentiate f(-x)=f(x); chain rule gives -f'(-x)=f'(x).
title: Course reference

question: Derive the Laplace transform of the constant one for t>=0.
reference: 1/s, region Re(s)>0.
title: Course reference

question: Prove that a real square matrix with a nonzero determinant is invertible.
reference: Use adjugate identity A adj(A)=det(A)I; divide by nonzero determinant.
title: Course reference

question: Derive the voltage across a charging RC capacitor from zero under a DC step V.
reference: v_C(t)=V(1-exp(-t/(RC))) under the ideal series RC assumptions, with time constant RC.
title: Course reference
